description: Team from Casablanca, Morocco. We chose a storytelling challenge to share the story of NASA's equipment left on the Moon and Mars in a creative and simple way for everyone.
summary: We built a Planetary Heritage Atlas: an interactive website that documents abandoned places on Earth and in space as heritage, not waste. Using NASA Earth data and satellite imagery, we show how nature reclaims abandoned cities, mines and stations, and why they must be preserved. Users can explore places, see their stories, and understand their ecological and cultural value. Our project addresses the challenge by turning forgotten places into a living archive for education, memory and conservation.
details: Our website is a Planetary Heritage Atlas. It works as an interactive map and archive: each abandoned place has a story, photos, location and what happened to it. We used NASA Earth Observatory and Landsat imagery to show change over time and how nature reclaims these sites. We built it with HTML, CSS and JavaScript hosted on GitHub Pages. It is creative because it reframes abandonment as heritage. The impact is educational: it helps people care about forgotten places, learn about climate and land use, and inspire preservation instead of demolition.
